description: Prototype gallery concept: Git Graph Timeline.
title: Gallery Prototype A | Git Graph Timeline

hero.title: Git Graph
hero.subtitle: Timeline Gallery
hero.lead: This direction turns your life and work path into a visual commit history. It is the strongest option if you want the page to feel technical, personal, and structured around milestones that later link out to deeper pages.
chips: Easy to extend with future branches

aside.title: How This Prototype Reads
aside.copy: The central line behaves like a repository history. Small nodes can represent transitions, while larger cards can later hold real achievements, publications, posters, awards, or project breakouts.

section_heading.title: Sample Git History
section_heading.copy: Temporary milestones only. Real text, images, dates, and target links can be replaced later once the layout direction is approved.

rows.title: 10th Standard
rows.copy: A first major checkpoint in the story. This card would later hold a short note, one image, and a redirect to a deeper page or achievement container.

rows.title: 12th Standard
rows.copy: The layout supports a short narrative under each checkpoint. Later this could show rank, interests, formative work, or the start of a specific research direction.

rows.title: College
rows.copy: This is a good spot for a wider branch in the future: coursework, early research exposure, clubs, internships, and role shifts can all split out from this node.

rows.title: Projects During College
rows.copy: This card format can later expand into project tags, short impact notes, posters, demos, or links to individual containers for each major build or experiment.

rows.title: Joined PhD
rows.copy: The latest and most important node can be visually larger later, with publications, posters, active themes, and onward links to work pages, PDFs, or a living research log.

footer: this version is optimized for a technical narrative. It will work especially well if later you want branch lines, year filters, or links out to research and project sub-pages.
